data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Rephael means 'God's Healer'. In the Bible, Rephael is mentioned as one of the 72 angels who visited Jesus during His temptation. He is also considered a patron saint of healing.

in_hebrew.name: רפאל
in_hebrew.meaning: אל רפא רפה אלקים ורפא לנפשי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רפאל הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אל רפא רפה אלקים ורפא לנפשי', שם שמקורו בשפה העברית ומשמעותו קשורה לרפואה ולשמיים. השם מורכב מ'רפא' שפירושו לרפא, ומ'אל' שפירושו אלוהים. השם רפאל מופיע בתנ'ך כדמות של מלאך הרפואה והשמיים.

in_greek.name: Ραφαήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ραφαήλ είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Θεός ίαμαί έλεγε και Ραφαήλ', δηλαδή Θεός που θεραπεύει. Ο Ραφαήλ αναφέρεται στην Αγία Γραφή ως άγγελος που θεραπεύει και προστατεύει.

in_latin.name: Raphael
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Raphael significat 'Deus sanavit vel Deus sanat', quod nomen ex Hebraeo origine venit. In traditione christiana, Raphael est angelus medicorum et sanationis.

in_english.name: Rephael
in_english.meaning: God heals or God has healed
in_english.long_meaning: The name Rephael originates from Hebrew roots, specifically from 'Rapa' meaning 'to heal' and 'El' meaning 'God'. It signifies 'God heals' or 'God has healed'. In the biblical context, Raphael is known as one of the seven archangels and is associated with healing and protection. The name holds significant spiritual meaning across Christian cultures, symbolizing divine healing and care.

biblical_reference.note: In the Book of Tobit, Raphael is the name of an archangel who heals Tobit's blindness and accompanies Tobias on a journey.

saint_reference.note: Saint Raphael is venerated as an archangel in the Roman Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox Church, and other Christian traditions, often invoked for healing and protection.

data.spiritual_significance: In Christian belief, Michael is considered a powerful protector and defender of God's people and is often invoked during times of spiritual conflict or warfare.

historical_references.reference: The Old Testament mentions an angel named Rephael, who is identified as one of the seven angels who hold the seven bowls of God's wrath. This identification is found in the Book of Revelation (Revelation 15:1-8). The time period for this reference is the late 1st century AD, during which the Book of Revelation was written.
historical_references.context: The Book of Revelation is the last book of the New Testament and is a prophetic work that describes a vision of the end times. The seven angels with the seven bowls represent the seven last plagues that God will pour out on the earth to bring about the end of the world as we know it.

historical_references.reference: In medieval Christian tradition, Rephael is considered the patron saint of the repentant sinner, the healer, and those who are sick. This role is a reflection of the biblical Rephael's association with healing and restoration. The time period for this reference is the Middle Ages, during which the cult of saints and their associated patronages became an important part of Christian practice.
historical_references.context: Medieval Christians believed that saints in heaven could intercede on behalf of the living, and that they had special powers that could be invoked through prayer. Rephael, as a powerful and healing angel, became a popular figure for those seeking spiritual guidance and physical healing.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern times, the Christian name Rephael (Raphael) has gained popularity beyond its religious context. The name Raphael is often associated with angelic beings and supernatural entities due to its biblical origins. In pop culture, Raphael is a common name for angels in television series such as Angel and Supernatural. In fantasy literature, Raphael is a popular name for divine beings in novels featuring angels and other supernatural creatures. In gaming, Raphael is a common name for characters in RPG and MMORPG games, reflecting the influence of religious and mythological traditions on fantasy and role-playing genres.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Rephael in Dublin, Ireland credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Rephael, which means "God's Healer". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Rephael is a Hebrew name meaning "God heals". It is often associated with the archangel Raphael, who is said to have the power to heal and protect. In Christian mythology, Raphael is one of the seven archangels, representing healing and mercy.
